name: fastfetch
summary: Fast system-information tool (neofetch successor) with a JSONC config: custom logo (ASCII file, raw, or an image over sixel/kitty/iterm/chafa), module list, per-module format strings and colors.
configFormat: JSONC (config.jsonc) with a JSON schema; presets via -c <name>
startupCostMs: Measured 2026-11-23, Windows 11, fastfetch 2.71.0 via scoop shim, median of 10 runs: default config 41 ms; a 3-module custom config 34 ms; `fastfetch --version` 47 ms; an empty `cmd /c rem` 23 ms. A working 11-module dossier config in the Eclipse preset is documented at ~55 ms. Slow modules are network ones (PublicIp, Weather, Wifi, LocalIp) and GPU/Packages on some systems: leave them out of a shell-start config.

windows.notes: Search paths printed by `fastfetch --list-config-paths` on Windows 11 (2.71.0): ~/.config/fastfetch/, ~/fastfetch/, <Git>/mingw64/etc/fastfetch/ (if Git for Windows is installed), %PROGRAMDATA%/fastfetch/, %APPDATA%/fastfetch/, %LOCALAPPDATA%/fastfetch/. In JSONC paths use %ENVVAR% syntax; ~ expansion needs v2.41.0+. Image logos use the platform image framework (WIC), no ImageMagick.

install.notes: Debian 13+ and Ubuntu 25.04+ only (README); not in Ubuntu 24.04 (use the project's release .deb or a PPA).

linux.notes: Image logos (sixel, kitty, chafa) need fastfetch built with ImageMagick and/or chafa support; check `fastfetch --list-features`.

install-init.notes: Install, config path, run on shell start with a quiet-variable guard.

logo.notes: ASCII/ANSI text file with $1..$9 color slots, raw files, images via sixel/kitty/kitty-direct/iterm/chafa.

theme.notes: Key/title/separator colors and bar/percent colors; hex or ANSI names.
